name: Make sushi rolls
blurb: Home sushi is a rice skill, not a fish skill. Get the rice right — seasoned, cooled correctly, at the right texture — and everything else is assembly.
gear: Short-grain sushi rice, rice vinegar, sugar, salt
A bamboo rolling mat and cling film
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, cook it properly, then fold through the vinegar seasoning while hot, using a cutting motion so the grains stay intact.
Cool the rice to body temperature, covered with a damp cloth. Never refrigerate it.
Prepare fillings: cucumber, avocado, cooked prawn or high-quality fish — and read up on what is safe raw before using any raw fish.
Lay nori shiny side down, spread a thin, even layer of rice leaving a clear strip at the far edge, and place the filling in a line.
Roll with the mat, applying even pressure and tucking the near edge under the filling to start a tight cylinder.
Cut with a very sharp wet knife, wiping between each cut.
tips: Too much rice is the universal beginner error. A thin layer rolls far better.
Only use fish sold as safe for raw consumption, and keep it cold throughout.
Wet hands stop the rice sticking to everything, including you.
proof: Tight, even rolls that hold together when cut, with well-seasoned rice at the right texture.
